(1) the dynamics of complex living systems are best described by multi-scale models that include both the dynamics of individual components and the dynamics of interactions between components; and (2) the dynamics of individual biological components are often best described by a combination of deterministic and stochastic processes, with the relative importance of these two processes changing with the scale of the system.
the complexity and dynamics of biological systems is explained by multi-scale models that describe the system's dynamics, and that the system's dynamics is the basis of its behaviour.
the dynamics of complex systems can be explained in terms of the interactions between the parts and the emergent behaviour of the system as a whole.

the development of dynamic mathematical models of biological processes.
the dynamics and multi-scaling of complex living systems.
the dynamics, multi-scalability and emergence of biological systems.
